name: ITOCHU
headline: A Japanese trading house whose lowest-cost iron-ore and coking-coal mines carry its profits.
what_short: Japanese trading house with mining and retail
what_it_does: ITOCHU is a Japanese trading company with many businesses. Its Metals & Minerals division, a low-cost iron-ore and coking-coal producer, is the part that carries the analysis. It also owns FamilyMart, the convenience store chain, since 2018.
why_it_passed: Its iron-ore and coking-coal mines hold the lowest-cost position, which it kept through a full commodity cycle.
Its own return on shareholders' equity ran from 21.8% in fiscal 2022 down to 14.6% in fiscal 2026.
Its borrowing is moderate: net debt to equity fell from 0.54 to 0.46.
The accounts raised no suspicion and no doubt about honesty was found.
why_not_now: At ¥2,155 a share, the price is above the top of the analysis's value range (¥1,466 to ¥1,902). A buyer would earn about 3.1% to 3.8% a year in cash, below both the roughly 10% the analysis requires and the 4.136% a 30-year Japanese government bond pays.
watch: Cleaner steelmaking is a twenty-year threat to the iron-ore and coking-coal business, and its coal part is weak.
The price of its raw materials swings, so the cash it produces is hard to pin down.
It has net debt of about ¥3.6 trillion and a pending purchase of Dentsu Soken that the analysis valued as if closed; management's ability was weighed against.
